description: Modulation matrix with twelve signal inputs and sixteen mix outputs, a depth knob at every crossing, and a row of sixteen control knobs that set the base levels and edit one row at a time

params.text: Sets the base level of its column when no row is selected, and the depth of the selected row's crossing while a Select button is held
Sets how much its row's input reaches that column's Mix output, -1 to 1
While it is held, the sixteen Control knobs jump to that row's depths so they can be edited; letting go brings the base values back

inputs.text: Sets the range the sixteen Control knobs work over: a 16-channel polyphonic cable sets each column separately, and with no cable every column runs to 5V in bipolar mode or 10V in unipolar
One of the twelve signals to be mixed; its channel count helps set the polyphony of every Mix output

outputs.text: The base level of its column plus each input times that column's depth knob, clamped to -12V and 12V
The sixteen base values of the Control knobs on sixteen polyphonic channels
The sixteen current values of the Control knobs on sixteen polyphonic channels, which differ from the base values while a row is selected

notes: the module is built to be driven by a MIDI controller: sixteen physical knobs onto the Control row and twelve buttons onto the Select column, mapped with something like stoermelder's MIDI-CAT
a Mix output is only worked out when it has a cable, so unused columns cost nothing
the lamp beside a Select button shows which row is selected for editing
the polyphony of every Mix output is the largest channel count of the twelve signal inputs
menu: Reduce internal sample rate: 1x to 1024x — runs the matrix at a fraction of the sample rate, which costs much less processor time and is harmless on modulation signals
Latch buttons — changes the Select buttons from momentary to latching, which suits selecting a row with the mouse; only one row can be selected either way
Bipolar — switches the knobs between running -100% to 100% and 0 to 100%
Relative MIDI control mode — makes an incoming MIDI knob move the value relative to where it is, which stops the jump you get when a physical knob and the on-screen one disagree
